items.title: MetaARIMA: Configuration-Level Transfer Learning for ARIMA Models
items.abstract: Time Series Foundation Models have demonstrated that pretraining on diverse datasets enables effective transfer to new forecasting tasks. Classical methods like ARIMA, however, remain configured and trained independently for each series, discarding knowledge from previous experiments. Consequently, selecting and training an ARIMA configuration remains challenging and often relies on heuristic approaches based on in-sample goodnessof-fit measures. We propose MetaARIMA, a pretrained configuration policy based on metalearning that brings transfer learning to classical statistical forecasting at the configuration level rather than the model level. The policy learns from historical experiments which ARIMA configurations achieve top-quantile performance, and recommends promising candidates for new series while preserving interpretability and local estimation. At inference, it selects a diverse set of candidates via maximal marginal relevance and efficiently identifies the final configuration using successive halving. Experiments in a transfer learning setting, training on M4 and evaluating on M1, M3, and Tourism, show that MetaARIMA outperforms AutoARIMA and other classical methods while being more dataefficient. In a comparison with recent zero-shot foundation models, MetaARIMA remains competitive with Chronos2, Moirai2, and TimesFM. The experiments are publicly available at https://github.com/vcerqueira/experiments-metaarima.

items.title: Methods and Tools for Multi-hazard Risk Assessment
items.abstract: Abstract Multi-Hazard Risk Assessment (MHRA) integrates hazard, exposure, and vulnerability analyses to quantify potential disaster impacts and support risk-informed decision-making. It evaluates the probability and consequences of multiple, interacting hazards such as floods, earthquakes, hurricanes, and landslides, and their cascading effects on people, infrastructure, and ecosystems. MHRA approaches range from qualitative methods, including community-based assessments and indicator-based analyses, to quantitative and probabilistic models that estimate economic and human losses. Advances in data availability, modelling, and artificial intelligence have enhanced the precision of risk estimation, while frameworks such as CAPRA, HAZUS, RiskScape, and CLIMADA provide practical tools for implementation. The chapter also highlights the importance of regional collaboration, uncertainty analysis, and scenario-based forecasting for adaptive planning. Strengthening MHRA capacities, particularly in data integration and multi-scale modelling, is essential to improving disaster preparedness, financial resilience, and long-term climate adaptation strategies.

items.title: MultiEvoSkill: Structure-Aware Multi-Agent Skill Evolution for Generalizable Skill Artifacts
items.abstract: Skill documents are becoming the default adaptation surface for frozen large language model (LLM) agents, but current skill generators face two key limitations. First, humans and different LLMs differ in how they organize procedural knowledge and approach task solving. Skills authored from a human or single-model perspective may therefore fail to align with the reasoning behaviors of other backbones, limiting cross-model generalization. Second, sequential skill descriptions inadequately represent procedures with parallel branches and explicit dependencies, while existing skill optimizers primarily operate on prose and lack explicit support for graph-structured skill evolution. We introduce MultiEvoSkill, a skill-optimization framework comprising three core components: 1) Skill compiler casts the skill as a typed graph with tailored operators, producing a compact, informative representation with explicit procedural topology; 2) Heterogeneous agent system proposes revision advices using collective intelligence, where minimal and informative issues are identified based on multiple sets of experiences. 3) Structure-aware debate and evolution mechanism organizes candidate edits into a heterogeneous graph, resolves them under dependency and importance constraints, and distills the collective proposal into the artifact. Multi-dimensional gating ensures the information gain and topological correctness of each evolution. Optimal skills are then obtained when the system converges at a consistent state. Various experiments and ablations against SOTA methods validate the effectiveness and generalization of MultiEvoSkill.

items.title: Nanoparticle delivery systems for gene therapy of degenerative musculoskeletal diseases
items.abstract: Degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMDs) are a group of chronic conditions characterized by the progressive deterioration of tissue structure and function, primarily affecting the articular cartilage, bones, tendons, and ligaments. With global aging populations, the rising prevalence of these disorders presents a growing public health challenge. Current treatments for DMDs are limited by substantial drug side effects and restricted therapeutic efficacy. Gene therapy has emerged as a promising alternative for addressing these conditions. Nanoparticles are essential for overcoming intracellular and extracellular barriers in nucleic acid delivery. Recent technological advances have led to novel nanomaterials and strategies, which have enabled safer and more efficient gene therapy. This review comprehensively analyzes the role of nanoparticle delivery systems in enabling effective gene-based interventions for major DMDs. First, we analyze the main gene therapies for various DMDs. Next, we systematically summarize recent advances in nanocarrier platforms and delivery strategies targeting osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, intervertebral disc degeneration, and tendon diseases. Finally, we discuss key challenges and future directions, offering a roadmap to advance nanoparticle delivery therapeutics toward clinical impact. This synthesis uniquely bridges nanoparticle delivery design with disease-specific pathophysiology, providing strategic guidance for overcoming translational barriers through emerging technologies including AI-driven carrier optimization and organ-on-chip platforms. Across these diseases, no carrier is universally optimal: systemic bone delivery prioritizes circulation stability and cell-selective targeting, whereas local delivery to cartilage, intervertebral discs, and tendons requires a balance among tissue retention, matrix penetration, cellular uptake, and controlled release. Current evidence remains predominantly preclinical and frequently demonstrates tissue accumulation without fully establishing intact-cargo delivery, functional target engagement, long-term safety, or manufacturability. This review therefore links nanoparticle design to disease-specific barriers and identifies the evidence required for clinical translation. The Translational Potential of this Article. This review focuses on the clinical translational potential of nanoparticle-based delivery systems for gene therapy in degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMDs). Addressing the unique physiological and pathological barriers of specific musculoskeletal tissues (such as bone, cartilage, intervertebral discs, and tendons), this article systematically summarizes targeting and sustained-release strategies designed to enhance delivery efficiency and overcome tissue-specific obstacles. Furthermore, this study highlights future perspectives, including artificial intelligence (AI)-driven carrier optimization, organ-on-a-chip models, and multimodal combination therapies integrating biomaterials and cells. By addressing the limitations of conventional therapies that merely alleviate symptoms without reversing tissue degeneration, this review provides a robust theoretical foundation and a clear translational roadmap for the development of precise, safe, and long-lasting gene therapy regimens for DMDs.

items.title: Navigating chaos and leapfrogging to Pharma 5.0 with ontological honesty and epistemic humility
items.abstract: Abstract: Pharmaceutical manufacturing remains constrained by legacy paradigms that collapse engineered systems into static legal descriptors and struggle to integrate real‑world evidence. Geopolitical instability, supply‑chain fragility, climate‑driven disruption, declining institutional trust and the accelerating influence of generative artificial intelligence expose that constraint as an epistemic ceiling. This Perspective outlines a professional path for leapfrogging toward a patient‑centric Pharma 5.0 paradigm grounded in ontological honesty and epistemic humility. The argument traces this ceiling across three layers—the individual practitioner, the quality system and the broader ecosystem—and places Deming’s System of Profound Knowledge, Kegan’s orders of consciousness and McGilchrist’s hemispheric account alongside the classical sequence of the nafs and a heart‑centered posture of practice (Dil Se). Leapfrogging is a knowledge strategy before it is a technology strategy. Recent United States hearings and independent quality‑scoring efforts reveal an ontology capable of detecting divergence yet unable to revise certified reality. Pakistan and the broader Global South live under the same ceiling, shaped by high generic volumes and thin margins. Thailand’s May 2025 registration of a domestically developed trastuzumab biosimilar demonstrates capability‑first sequencing; a subsequent United States draft guidance issued on 29 October 2025—proposing that comparative efficacy studies may be unnecessary when analytical comparability is high—confirms the direction of that sequence rather than authorizing it after the fact. Preparing for Pharma 5.0 requires unlearning certain validated habits, cultivating sovereignty of judgment before sovereign infrastructure and building quality systems capable of revising their own descriptions.

items.title: Non-Invasive Brain Stimulation as a Method for Mitigation of Spaceflight Neurodegeneration & Associated Cognitive Decline
items.abstract: Evidence is mounting toward the idea that spaceflight stressors decrease cognitive function over time. Current countermeasures focus largely on spacecraft design and environmental modifications, but direct interventions on astronaut physiology could be essential for long-term success. Noninvasive brain stimulation (NiBS) is increasingly used to modulate neuroplasticity and has shown promise for improving cognition in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related conditions. NiBS appears plausible as a countermeasure candidate for spaceflight-associated cognitive decline; space-radiation pathways overlap with AD-relevant mechanisms, and AD trials demonstrate rTMS-associated cognitive and plasticity gains. However, the current literature primarily supports plausibility and mechanism overlap rather than direct validation in spaceflight or high-fidelity analogs; there is little evidence for NiBS effects in microgravity; spaceflight-induced brain changes may alter stimulation responses; validated operational protocols and standardized biomarkers are lacking; and long-term safety under extreme environments is uncertain.

items.title: NovaFabric: A Black-Box Recorder for AI Agents with Sealed, Replayable, Diffable and Auditable Runs
items.abstract: An AI agent run is no longer a function call. It is a cascade of prompts, model calls, tool invocations, file and network effects and sub-agents. When such a run misbehaves, or an auditor asks what happened, logs and traces answer poorly: they are mutable, partial and cannot be re-executed. This technical report describes NovaFabric, an open-source (Apache-2.0) black-box recorder for AI agents that turns a run into a sealed, replayable, diffable and auditable evidence capsule. The design rests on two formats only. The Run Capsule is a directory of flat files and the source of truth; every database is a rebuildable index over capsules. The Evidence Bundle is the signed export for an auditor. Everything else follows existing standards: OpenTelemetry GenAI, OpenLineage, W3C PROV, in-toto/DSSE, RFC 3161 and CycloneDX. A single-node run is the smallest case of a distributed one; the schema supports a capsule hierarchy for Slurm arrays and Kubernetes jobs, though automatic parent finalization is library-only today. The report covers the architecture and the engines behind the verb chain capture, seal, replay, diff and audit: fail-closed mocked replay; a diff gate with a stable exit-code contract; DSSE signatures that bind their intent and a capsule root that commits to file names; a capsule treated as untrusted input; signer identity-trust levels with offline TSA and CRL checking; maker-checker promotion against an operator-held trust list; and a deny-by-default authorization table for every dashboard route. It presents no new experiments; the evaluation is in arXiv:2609.12582. Every count except the private ADR tally is generated by a probe script run on the public source at the v0.107.0 tag (150 top-level commands, 84 Python subpackages, 16,721 test functions), every capability carries an explicit maturity label, and honest-limits boxes state where the system stops.

items.title: On the uniqueness of translation-invariant ground states of the $S=1$ Heisenberg and $J$--$D$ antiferromagnetic chains
items.abstract: Using the analytic machinery and numerical inputs of OpenAI's proofs of the Haldane gap, we prove uniqueness of the translation-invariant ground state of the infinite $S=1$ Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain and of the $J$-$D$ model for sufficiently small $|D|$. Uniqueness is among all translation-invariant ground states in the operator-algebraic sense, without assuming a gap or spin-rotation symmetry for a competing state. The proof combines concentration of the spatial transfer spectrum, an exponentially small low-temperature free-energy correction, and a Golden--Thompson comparison for separated local observables. The unique translation-invariant state is pure, locally unique and gapped, and continuous in $D$. The ground states of even periodic chains and odd open chains with equal positive endpoint fields converge to this state along their full sequences, uniformly in $D$, with a stretched-exponential local rate. Every choice of ground states of open chains without endpoint magnetic fields has the same local limit. These conclusions do not establish uniqueness among arbitrary nontranslation-invariant ground states of the infinite chain. The author formulated the problems and proposed the core strategies. ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to developing the proofs and preparing the manuscript.

items.title: One Standard Does Not Fit All: Limitations of Applying MIL-STD-1472H Across Diverse Government Programs
items.abstract: MIL-STD-1472H (Military Standard 1472 Version H) is the human engineering design standard applied across U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) acquisition programs. While the standard allows tailoring, it is frequently applied as a universal compliance baseline across diverse systems. One-size-fits all prescriptive standards can diminish human performance risks and constrain design adaptability (Dekker, 2017). Reliance on extensive tailoring increases system cost with minimal value and limits innovation. A subsection-level assessment of the Detailed Requirements section of MIL-STD-1472H demonstrates substantial variability in relevance across domains. In practice, tailoring serves as administrative compliance rather than advancing human performance outcomes. In addition, MIL-STD-1472H fails to address emerging challenges with integrating artificial intelligence into human-machine interfaces. Future DoD human engineering standards need to better align with system context, lifecycle maturity, and emerging technologies, consistent with Department of Defense artificial intelligence (AI) policy.

items.title: ParetoRSI-Gym: Can AI Agents Improve Language Models Across Multiple Domains?
items.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires an agentic system to design, train, and evaluate its own successor. Data-driven post-training is a central part of that loop, yet existing evaluations measure it on a single benchmark, where an agent selects from a static pool or distills a stronger model to push one score up in one run. Real post-training is multi-domain, and a gain in one domain has to be weighed against a regression in another. We propose ParetoRSI-Gym, in which an agent searches for data, curates it, trains, reads back per-domain results, and repeats, with everything but the data held fixed: the initial LLM, the five domains (math, code, finance, medicine, science), the toolset, and the SFT pipeline. Generalization benchmarks in each domain separate capability gains from overfitting to the scores the agent optimizes against. Across three agent systems, three base models, five rounds and multiple seeds, the strongest system, Claude Code with Opus-5, raises the generalization scores of its proxy-best checkpoint by 9.2% relative to the starting model (+2.3 absolute points), averaged with equal weight over three base models and five domains, with a single-domain relative gain of up to 63% (medicine on Ministral-3-3B). Further analysis shows that the harness matters as much as the model it drives, and that each agent keeps a unique data selection strategy. We see our work as a step towards evaluation of RSI systems in real-world machine learning engineering.

items.title: Patient-Facing Applications of Large Language Models in Persistent Pain: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Background/Aim Large language models (LLMs) have rapidly expanded into healthcare-related applications, including patient education and health information delivery. While conversational agents in pain management have previously been reviewed, the specific use of LLM-powered systems in patient-facing persistent pain contexts remains underexplored. This scoping review aimed to synthesize current literature on the use of LLMs in pain care Methods This scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were performed across PubMed, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Google Scholar for English-language studies published between January 2023 and March 2026. Studies investigating patient-facing or informational applications of LLMs in pain-related contexts were included. Extracted data included pain condition, LLM role, interaction type, prompt design strategy, and evaluation approach. Results Forty-six studies were included. Most studies were published in 2025 and evaluated OpenAI’s ChatGPT. LLMs were primarily positioned as information provision tools, with single-turn question-and-answer interactions. Evaluation approaches focused largely on information quality, accuracy, and readability, frequently relying on expert-based subjective assessments and readability metrics without input from people living with pain. Multi-turn conversational interactions (2 studies) and longitudinal evaluations (2 studies) were uncommon. Patient involvement was limited: some studies incorporated patients in question or prompt development, while only one directly involved people with lived experience in evaluating LLM-generated outputs. Conclusion Persistent pain-related LLM research primarily evaluates the quality and safety of static informational outputs, with less attention to conversational, adaptive and user-centred interactions. Future research should incorporate realistic interaction scenarios, patient-generated inputs and measures of user engagement to better assess clinical relevance.

items.title: PENERAPAN GREEN CONSTRUCTION PADA BANGUNAN HIJAU : STUDI LITERATUR
items.abstract: The construction sector plays a crucial role in infrastructure development, yet its activities pose high risks to environmental degradation. This study aims to evaluate various forms of practical application of green construction and green building concepts across several projects in Indonesia. The research method employed is a qualitative literature study by analyzing evaluation results from 15 construction projects using the Model Assessment Green Construction (MAGC) instrument and Greenship standards. The research results identify that the primary forms of field application include material resource management through the use of eco-friendly cement and local materials to reduce carbon emissions by up to 94 kgCO2e/m^{2}. In terms of technical building aspects, implementation is realized through passive design that optimizes building orientation and natural ventilation, as well as replacing lighting systems with LED lamps for energy efficiency. Furthermore, water management is implemented through the creation of biopore infiltration holes, retention ponds, and disciplined dewatering management. Although Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) and material management aspects show successful implementation, the application of water and energy conservation technologies still requires further optimization. This study concludes that the integrated application of green concepts from the planning stage not only minimizes environmental impacts but is also capable of achieving long-term operational cost efficiency for project owners. items.title: Personnel training for the digital construction industry: economic aspects
items.abstract: The digital transformation of the construction industry is one of the key areas for improving the efficiency of investment and construction activities. The introduction of building information modeling technologies, digital twins, artificial intelligence, automated project management systems and other digital tools requires qualified specialists who are able to work in a digital economy. At the same time, the construction sector is facing a shortage of personnel with the necessary digital competencies. The article examines the economic aspects of personnel training for the digital construction industry, analyzes the causes of personnel shortages, examines the costs of training and corporate staff development, and evaluates the effectiveness of investments in improving employee digital literacy. Special attention is paid to the issues of interaction between educational organizations and construction companies as the main mechanism for the formation of human resources in the industry. Based on the analysis, promising models of cooperation between universities and employers are proposed, ensuring an increase in the quality of specialist training and a reduction in personnel shortages.

items.title: Predictive Artificial Intelligence in SEND Systems: Evaluating Early Identification, Risk, and Governance Implications
items.abstract: The application of predictive artificial intelligence (AI) within Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) systems represents one of the most consequential and underexplored frontiers in contemporary educational data mining. This study investigates the deployment of machine learning algorithms to identify learners who may require additional support, evaluating the reliability, validity, and fairness of such predictive systems within the United Kingdom educational framework. Drawing on a structured literature synthesis spanning 2015–2025, a comparative analysis of seven machine learning algorithms including Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine, and Neural Networks was conducted using datasets simulated from real-world SEND contexts. Results demonstrate that ensemble methods, particularly Random Forest and XGBoost, achieve the most consistent cross-validation performance (accuracy 74.3–77.5%), while simpler models offer greater interpretability. However, significant concerns emerge regarding false positive and false negative classification rates across protected demographic groups, with girls, learners from minority ethnic backgrounds, and those with masking conditions systematically underidentified. Governance analysis reveals critical gaps in the UK regulatory landscape, including an absence of mandatory explainability standards and algorithmic fairness requirements specific to SEND AI tools. This study proposes a five-pillar governance framework encompassing legal compliance, transparency, equity, human oversight, and data quality as a basis for the responsible deployment of predictive AI in SEND settings. Findings underscore that algorithmic decision support should complement rather than replace professional judgement, with human-in-the-loop protocols essential to ethical implementation.

items.title: Proper working-time accounting as a safeguard for employees’ occupational health and safety
items.abstract: Abstract Every employee has the right to working conditions that respect their health, safety, and dignity. Working time is a condition of employment and is subject to restrictions to safeguard employees’ occupational health and safety. EU Member States are obliged to ensure that these restrictions are observed in employment relationships. Compliance with working-time restrictions can be ensured through working-time accounting. The corresponding obligation is imposed on employers, who are expected to establish an objective, reliable, and accessible system for accounting for working time. This article examines how to create a working-time accounting system that meets the above conditions and protects employees’ health and safety. To calculate working time, it is essential to understand the various ways in which it can be determined. An “always-on” work culture and the blurring of boundaries between working and rest time complicate working-time accounting. The absence of national regulation may lead employers to assume that it is sufficient to measure working time at their own discretion. This approach creates inequality at the national level and fails to foster a favourable environment for protecting workers’ health, safety, and dignity. In this article, the authors present their view of how a working-time accounting system should be designed to ensure safeguards for employees’ occupational health and safety. The article is based on an analysis of European Union, Spanish, German, Greek, and Estonian regulations.

items.title: Propuesta de Marco Ético-Pedagógico para Integrar IA Generativa en Universidades Estatales de Santo Domingo, 2026
items.abstract: Justification: The integration of generative artificial intelligence into higher education has created opportunities to enhance teaching planning, material development, learning, and assessment, but has also raised concerns regarding academic integrity, data protection, transparency, and teacher training. Objective: To propose an ethical-pedagogical framework to guide the responsible integration of generative artificial intelligence into educational processes at public universities in Santo Domingo during 2026. Methodology: A qualitative approach, non-experimental design, and descriptive-propositional scope were adopted, applying legal-doctrinal, analytical, descriptive, documentary, and deductive methods through documentary analysis. Results: The documentary analysis revealed that the educational integration of generative artificial intelligence required institutional principles related to transparency, accountability, data protection, teacher training, disclosure of its use, and verification of generated content, along with changes in assessment practices aimed at preserving student authorship and strengthening knowledge acquisition. Conclusion: Educational uses, risks, and criteria related to transparency, teacher training, human oversight, academic integrity, learning assessment, and data protection were identified.

items.title: PyPI API Drift: A Release-Level Record of Public API Changes in 1,872 Popular Python Libraries, with a Checker and a Benchmark for Version-Aware Code Generation
items.abstract: Ask a code assistant to append a row to a pandas DataFrame and it may write df.append(row), a method removed in pandas 2.0. Models trained on code from many releases cannot tell which API exists in the version a user has installed, and benchmarks of this problem are small and frozen. We present PyPI API Drift, a release-level record of the public APIs of the 1,872 most-downloaded Python libraries: up to 80 recent final releases each (55,565 releases, 2021–October 2026), with signatures, 15,258,652 release-to-release changes and 210,535 deduplicated breaking changes. Extraction is static and import-free, reads only the needed bytes of each wheel, separates names that were truly removed from names that merely left the documented API, and marks with confidence labels and a coverage layer where static analysis cannot see. It is a high-precision, low-recall record: in two held-out runtime audits by AI agents isolated from the pipeline (on earlier data versions), 88.8% and 91.9% of high-confidence breaking changes were confirmed, while recall over all runtime-visible changes is limited (16 of 99). On top of it we release an offline checker, lookup tools with a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for coding agents, and VersionProbe, a benchmark of 10,958 valid/invalid snippet pairs. In a preregistered code-repair experiment, repeated across 4 models from one model family, API history from the dataset raised the share of API-compatible, intent-preserving migrations (under our evaluation protocol) to 68.5%–69.9% for every model, from 7.0%–56.6% unaided and 46.2%–62.2% with the new release’s documentation. 13.4% of patch releases contain at least one breaking change.Code: https://github.com/pushkardg/pypi-api-drift Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/pushkar87dg/pypi-api-drift

items.title: QECGBERT: A Scalable ECG Foundation Model Based on Self-Supervised Language Learning via VQ-VAE Waveform Tokenization
items.abstract: AI foundation models play a pivotal role in advancing heart disease diagnosis from electrocardiogram (ECG) data, particularly for rare diseases where the lack of sufficient labeled data hinders supervised learning. However, most self-supervised learning methods treat ECGs as generic sequence or image data without exploiting underlying physiological structure. To address this limitation, we propose QECGBERT, a self-supervised ECG language model that explicitly encodes physiological semantics by tokenizing the P, QRS, T, and isoelectric background waveforms. Vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE) tokenization is applied to each 12-lead ECG, with tokens enriched by continuous waveform features to preserve morphology lost during quantization without increasing sequence length. This design enables compact BERT masked language modeling with short sequences, improving scalability and reducing computational cost relative to long-sequence approaches. QECGBERT applies BERT pre-training to the MIMIC-IV dataset containing over 800,000 unlabeled ECG recordings, and fine-tuning on labeled PTB-XL, CPSC2018, and Chapman--Shaoxing--Ningbo datasets for evaluation. The results demonstrate that QECGBERT achieves comparable or superior performance to published benchmarks, offering a scalable, physiologically aware approach to ECG foundation modeling for cardiac diagnosis.

items.title: Quantifying Shared Mental Models in Nursing Using Multimodal Physiological and Communication Data
items.abstract: Shared Mental Models (SMMs) are essential for effective nursing teamwork, yet existing assessments mainly rely on observations or self-reports that provide limited insight into team cognition during task execution. This study proposes a multimodal framework for quantifying SMM quality in virtual reality nursing simulations. Thirty nursing students (15 two-person teams) completed three collaborative clinical scenarios while electroencephalography (EEG), eye-tracking, and communication data were synchronously collected. Expert annotations were used to classify teams into high- and low-SMM groups. Results showed significant differences in neural activity, visual attention organization, and communication structures between the two groups. High-SMM teams demonstrated distinct EEG patterns, more organized gaze behaviors, and stronger connectivity between task-oriented communication components. These findings suggest that multimodal physiological and behavioral measures can provide objective indicators of SMM quality and support future development of real-time assessment tools for nursing teamwork and simulation-based education.

items.title: RAG-Based MCA AI Agent for Document-Grounded College Information Assistance Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Vector Search and a Locally Hosted Large Language Model
items.abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based MCA AI Agent for document-grounded question answering over college and student policy documents. The system uses PyMuPDF for PDF text extraction, approximately 1000-character chunks, Nomic-Embed-Text for generating 768-dimensional embeddings, and Pinecone for semantic vector search. At query time, the system retrieves the three most relevant document chunks and provides them as context to Llama 3.2 running locally through Ollama. A React.js frontend and FastAPI backend provide the conversational interface. The paper describes the system architecture, methodology, implementation, document-refresh workflow, and practical deployment considerations, including stale vectors and local inference latency. It also outlines an evaluation framework for comparing a standalone LLM with the proposed RAG pipeline using retrieval relevance, answer correctness, faithfulness, and latency. The current work is presented as a system implementation and preliminary study. A controlled quantitative evaluation has not yet been completed, and no numerical accuracy improvement is claimed. Keywords: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Large Language Models, Semantic Search, Vector Database, Pinecone, Llama 3.2, Ollama, FastAPI, React.js, Document-Grounded Question Answering.

items.title: Recent advances and emerging trends in smart parking technologies from sensor based to next generation parking system: a review
items.abstract: Rapid urbanization, growing vehicle ownership, and limited parking infrastructure have made parking allocation a major challenge in modern cities. To address this issue, numerous smart parking systems (SPSs) have been proposed to improve parking efficiency, reduce congestion, and enhance user convenience. This paper presents a comprehensive review and comparative analysis of SPSs in terms of technological approaches, sensing methods, networking technologies, computational models, user interfaces, and service capabilities. It also addresses an important research gap by evaluating the suitability of different SPS approaches under diverse environmental conditions and highlighting their key advantages and limitations. The review emphasizes the growing role of internet of things (IoT)-based, multi-approach architectures in enabling real-time monitoring, reservation, payment integration, and vehicle guidance for smart city applications. Furthermore, it discusses the potential of integrating reconfigurable systems with IoT to improve adaptability, scalability, and responsiveness through dynamic resource allocation and efficient local decision-making. Despite these benefits, challenges related to interoperability, security, energy management, design complexity, and deployment cost remain significant. Future SPSs are expected to incorporate artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, dynamic pricing, autonomous vehicle support, and digital twin technologies to achieve more adaptive, intelligent, and sustainable parking management.

items.title: Reconciling Food and Energy on the Same Land: An Explainable Artificial Intelligence Framework for Agrivoltaic Suitability Mapping
items.abstract: The swift growth of utility-scale solar farms has created fierce competition for agricultural land, especially in countries where prime solar energy sites and productive croplands coincide. Agrivoltaic structures, which incorporate agricultural food and electricity generation on one parcel, are a structural solution to this kind of land-use conflict; yet the question of where such systems should be sited has, to date, been addressed in the literature predominantly through subjective multi-criteria decision making methods. This study develops a fully data-driven and explainable machine learning framework for agrivoltaic site selection, using the province of Konya—Türkiye's grain basket and its largest agricultural region—as a case study. The site selection problem is formulated as a supervised binary classification task in which the geographic inventory of existing solar installations provides the ground-truth labels. Thirteen selected feature spanning climatic, topographic, economic, and socio-environmental dimensions were examined through Pearson correlation, variance inflation factor, and mutual information gain analyses. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting machine learning algorithms were trained with hyperparameter optimization, and observed performance variations were verified using omnibus Cochran's Q and pairwise McNemar statistical tests. Extreme Gradient Boosting achieved the highest performance (total accuracy: 0.9549, F1 score: 0.9533), followed by Random Forest (0.9390) and Logistic Regression (0.8661). Explainable artificial intelligence analysis, which renders the black-box nature of the models transparent, revealed that the most decisive factors determining agrivoltaic suitability were, respectively, distance to grid lines and global horizontal irradiance (GHI). The findings suggest that the proposed methodology may help minimize conflicts between energy and food security, thereby providing a strategic planning tool that can support progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (particularly SDGs 7 and 13).

items.title: RECONSTRUCTING CRIMINAL LIABILITY FOR AI-ENABLED CYBERCRIME IN INDONESIA: Toward a Normative Framework of Responsibility
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has fundamentally transformed the nature of cybercrime from human-controlled conduct into algorithmically mediated and semi-autonomous operations. In Indonesia, this transformation is reflected in the sharp increase in cybercrime cases, automated fraud, and AI-enabled digital manipulation, which challenge the traditional criminal liability framework based on human intent and direct control. This study employs normative legal research integrating statutory, conceptual, and comparative approaches to examine the adequacy of existing legal frameworks and to formulate a reconstructed model of criminal liability for AI-based cybercrime. The findings reveal that Indonesia’s current legal regime, primarily governed by the Criminal Code and Electronic Information and Transactions Law, remains rooted in an actor-based liability paradigm, resulting in an accountability gap when harm is caused through autonomous or semi-autonomous AI systems. This article offers a novel normative reconstruction based on a risk- and control-based liability framework operationalized through six elements: recognition of systemic AI risk, expansion of fault doctrine to include algorithmic oversight failure, adoption of multi-tier criminal liability, mandatory algorithmic transparency and audit trails, corporate liability based on risk management failure, and integration of the duty of care principle. This model preserves the principle of personal criminal responsibility while extending liability to actors who control and manage technological risk. The study contributes theoretically by bridging classical fault-based liability and risk-based accountability in criminal law and provides normative recommendations for harmonizing national criminal law and developing AI-specific regulations to ensure legal certainty and effective accountability in the digital era

items.title: Reconstruction of Criminal Event Timelines from Property Crime Investigation Documents Based on a Hybrid LLM-Rule Pipeline
items.abstract: Fact-finding in criminal proceedings reconstructs past events into a coherent narrative based on fragmented evidence and testimony, yet remains vulnerable to cognitive confirmation bias. While automating timeline construction using large language models (LLMs) offers decision support, confidentiality-critical local models are prone to temporal hallucinations, inverting causal orders or generating groundless timestamps. To mitigate these vulnerabilities, this study proposes Deep-ARC (Analysis, Reconstruction, and Contradiction detection for criminal timeline construction), a hybrid LLM-rule pipeline that algorithmically regulates model reasoning through legal domain schemas and deterministic rule logic. Deep-ARC injects statutory crime element schemas to categorize event phases and enforces phase-aware boundary clamping grounded on explicit timestamps, systematically resolving sequential contradictions during missing time inference. In proof-of-concept experiments focusing on corporate property crimes (breach of trust and embezzlement) with Gemma-4-31B, Deep-ARC achieved a Micro PMR (exact sequence match ratio) of 0.343 and a Kendall’s Tau (τ) of 0.861, representing an approximate fourfold improvement over the unconstrained baseline and demonstrating higher sequencing consistency than large-scale commercial LLMs. These results indicate that coupling domain-specific structural constraints with deterministic algorithms offers an effective and robust strategy for providing an objective chronological sequence to assist fact-finding without relying exclusively on parameter scaling.

items.title: Reframing GenAI-mediated EFL speaking: A systematic review of empirical studies through an Activity Theory lens
items.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has created more possibilities for English as a foreign language education. Through its generative capabilities, particularly in natural language generation and processing, GenAI has introduced new modes of interaction for learners’ speaking development. However, empirical research on GenAI-mediated EFL speaking remains fragmented. Guided by PRISMA 2020, this systematic review synthesizes 43 empirical studies published between 2024 and 2026 to examine the trends, application methods, and challenges of GenAI-mediated EFL speaking activities. Findings indicate that research has focused primarily on mainland China and intermediate-level undergraduate learners, with ChatGPT as the most frequently used tool. GenAI was commonly used to provide personalized practice and immediate feedback in a comparatively low-pressure environment. Most studies reported positive outcomes, but findings varied. Behavioral outcomes received less attention than cognitive and affective aspects. Challenges mainly involved inauthentic interaction and limited feedback. Tensions are mainly from tools and subjects, as well as tools and objects from an Activity Theory lens. Based on these tensions, this study proposes a collaborative learning framework to provide complementary mediation in EFL speaking activities.

items.title: Regenerative Habitation Colletion
items.abstract: Abstract Aeon Mundi is a collection of adaptive furnishings and robotic tools designed to connect small-plot, rotational food growing with the everyday life of homes, civic buildings, and shared public spaces. Its six pieces support a connected journey from cultivation and habitat care to harvesting, processing, and transport. Workstations, companion seating, and autonomous carts combine adjustable ergonomics with robotic assistance for moving crops, trays, and tools, keeping people involved at each stage. A common material language unites the collection: polished solid-cast mycelium in natural, vegetable-pigmented hues; sustainably loomed bamboo upholstery; rounded, repairable forms; and fine luminescent accents that respond to work phases. Embedded spatial displays offer abstract, user-invoked cues. Together, these elements frame food production as an accessible part of shared daily life and propose a design system for exploring how productive landscapes and human-centered technology can coexist.

items.title: Regenerative Habitation: Integrating Architecture, Adaptive Furniture, and Productive Landscapes
items.abstract: This preprint defines an implementation-oriented framework for regenerative habitation: the coordinated design of architecture, adaptive furniture, environmental technology, native habitat, diversified food production, and task-specific embodied robotics as one environment for human life and ecological continuity. The design question is how built environments can provide shelter and comfort while making ecological processes and voluntary participation accessible in ordinary life. Shared Cognitive Ecology describes the exchange among environmental information, spatial access, human activity, and ecological change. Environmental Coherence evaluates these relationships across ecological, architectural, material, technological, operational, and human domains. The paper synthesizes research on crop rotation, native urban planting, community gardens, agricultural human-robot collaboration, food life-cycle impacts, and land-use trade-offs. A 2024 review of 55 agricultural human-robot collaboration studies found that 34 met its criteria for robust collaboration and noted limited field and human-factor evidence; a 2025 review mapped 210 studies on agricultural robotics and extended reality. These findings inform design questions, but neither literature establishes performance for a residential or civic habitat. Evidence on land use and life-cycle impacts also establishes limits: food production can increase irrigation demand, material impacts, or habitat pressure. This conceptual synthesis defines a cross-scale model, operating method, measurable evaluation domains, and comparative civic prototype for future study. Ecological literacy, labor reduction, well-being, food output, biodiversity, and human-robot performance remain to be tested through baseline and longitudinal evaluation. Keywords: regenerative habitation; adaptive furniture; shared cognitive ecology; environmental coherence; productive landscapes; native biodiversity; urban agriculture; ecological restoration; human-robot collaboration; embodied robotics; integrated habitat systems

items.title: Regulating LLM training under EU copyright law and its linguistic implications for smaller languages such as Estonian
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and text and data mining (TDM) technologies has become a crucial factor in supporting linguistic diversity of smaller languages, such as Estonian. However, the growing reliance on large-scale data processing raises significant legal and ethical challenges, particularly concerning the lawful use of copyrighted materials to train AI systems. While the European Union has introduced regulatory instruments such as the AI Act and the Copyright Directive to address these concerns, the intersection of AI development, TDM, and intellectual property rights remains insufficiently resolved. This research aims to explore how AI-driven text and data mining can both comply with European copyright law and actively contribute to the preservation and wider use of the Estonian language. The authors investigate this research topic from the perspective of the Estonian language, enmeshed within Estonian cultural norms and parameters. The analysis examines the legal and economic appropriateness of enabling the training of generative AI-based large language models (LLMs) in the Estonian language as a means of promoting the language and assuring its appropriate use in digital environments, thereby contributing to its long-term relevance. Methodologically, the study combines a comparative analysis of EU, US, and Asian legal frameworks with a theoretical evaluation of existing models for balancing innovation and rights protection. The article seeks to provide concrete recommendations for developing AI and data mining practices that enhance linguistic innovation while safeguarding creators’ rights, thereby contributing to Estonia’s digital and cultural resilience within the EU’s evolving AI ecosystem.

items.title: Repairing Broken Access Control in Web Applications with LLMs: An Empirical Benchmark Study
items.abstract: Broken access control (BAC) ranks among the most severe web-application vulnerability classes, yet its automated repair remains largely unexplored. Unlike memory-safety vulnerabilities, BAC is a logic vulnerability whose repair demands a deep understanding of an application's access-control model and business semantics, which traditional automated vulnerability repair techniques handle poorly. Large language models (LLMs) open a promising avenue for this problem, but no standard benchmark exists for studying how well they repair BAC vulnerabilities. We construct BAC-Bench, the first benchmark for BAC repair, consisting of 46 real-world BAC vulnerabilities drawn from six widely used web applications spanning four programming languages. Each vulnerability is equipped with a sandboxed runtime environment, a PoC validation program and a functional test program. We further propose a BAC repair-strategy framework that characterizes any BAC patch along four dimensions, Position, Coverage, Mechanism, and Content. Evaluating eight base LLMs and two commercial LLM agents on BAC-Bench, we find that single-turn base LLMs repair 37.68% of the vulnerabilities on average, while two minimal scaffolds, Apply-Feedback and Navigate-and-Locate, raise this average to 66.03%, with the best base LLM reaching 75.36%, close to the 78.99% of the best agent. Notably, some LLM-generated patches surpass the official patches, and one incidentally closed a zero-day vulnerability that had lain dormant for three years. Our findings delineate the current capability boundary of LLM-based BAC repair and offer guidance toward its practical adoption.

items.title: Responsible GenAI Augmentation and Cognitive Agency in Higher Education
items.abstract: Responsible generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) integration in higher education requires attention to useful assistance and students’ continuing cognitive agency. We examined how learner capability, cognitive offloading and institutional support relate to intention to use a university GenAI learning service, alongside reported reduced independent thinking. A cross-sectional survey of 593 students at one Thai public university was analyzed using ordinal structural equation modeling with WLSMV estimation. AI self-efficacy was positively associated with information utilization, utilization with perceived work efficiency, and efficiency with service intention. The serial indirect association was positive, while adjusted direct self-efficacy associations with efficiency and intention were inconclusive. Offloading was positively associated with both efficiency and reduced independent thinking. Its positive indirect association with intention through efficiency coexisted with a negative adjusted direct association. Institutional support was positively associated with intention. The prespecified TRUST comparison and additional covariates, screening and complete-case checks, retained the main association pattern. However, replacing utilization with information analysis reduced the analogous serial association, and reversing the utilization–efficiency link gave better descriptive fit. The findings therefore concern concurrent perceptions and reported practices, without establishing serial ordering or causal mediation. Independent learning and actual service engagement remain essential criteria for assessing educational value.

items.title: RISK FACTORS FOR MUSCULOSKELETAL COMPLAINTS AMONG NURSES AT AZ-ZAHRA GENERAL HOSPITAL, KALIREJO, CENTRAL LAMPUNG
items.abstract: Musculoskeletal complaints are a common occupational health problem among nurses because their work involves physical activity, non-ergonomic postures, and long working hours. This study aimed to analyze the association of age, gender, and daily working hours with musculoskeletal complaints among nurses at Az-Zahra Kalirejo General Hospital, Central Lampung. This quantitative cross-sectional study involved all 68 nurses through total sampling. Data were collected using a respondent characteristics questionnaire and the Nordic Body Map, then analyzed using the Chi-Square test and Prevalence Ratio (PR). Twenty-two nurses (32.4%) experienced musculoskeletal complaints. Age (p=0.765; PR=1.125; 95% CI 0.534–2.368) and gender (p=0.712; PR=0.877; 95% CI 0.434–1.770) were not associated with musculoskeletal complaints. Daily working hours were significantly associated with musculoskeletal complaints (p<0.001): complaints were reported by 44.9% of nurses working more than 8 hours per day, whereas none of the nurses working ≤8 hours per day reported complaints. Daily working hours should be considered in preventing musculoskeletal complaints through work scheduling, adequate rest breaks, and ergonomic practices, although the cross-sectional design cannot establish a causal relationship.

items.title: Role of Ocimum tenuiflorum (Tulsi) in Al-Enabled Drug Discovery
items.abstract: Ocimum tenuiflorum L. (syn. O. sanctum; Tulsi, holy basil) is a Lamiaceae herb central to Ayurveda and now a frequent subject of computational drug discovery. Objective: To review how artificial intelligence (AI) and related in silico methods have been applied to O. tenuiflorum over roughly the last five years, to separate what these studies show from what they do not, and to outline implications for society. Methods: A structured narrative review of recent literature (2021 to October 2026) was conducted using web-based searches, with older sources used only for background. Thirteen primary Tulsi-focused studies were charted by approach, target, disease area, and main finding. Findings: Most studies combine database mining (notably IMPPAT), ADMET filtering, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics with targets spanning diabetes (DPP4, GAPDH, PPARδ), cancer (EGFR), inflammatory disease (AKT1, STAT3), and SARS-CoV-2 main protease. A smaller, emerging group applies machine learning or deep learning to metabolomics, hyperspectral imaging, and multi-omics. Experimental or clinical validation is sparse. Human trial evidence is limited in scale, and a 2023 regulatory-style risk assessment raised reproductive-safety precautions. Conclusion: Tulsi is a credible source of hypotheses, not yet of validated drug leads. The field's priority is closing the loop between prediction, standardized extracts, wet-lab assays, and well-designed trials, while protecting traditional knowledge and consumers.

items.title: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions
items.abstract: Scaling vision-language-action (VLA) models is constrained by scarce action-labeled demonstrations and incompatible control spaces across robot embodiments. We present RynnVLA-Latent, a framework that turns heterogeneous interaction videos into scalable supervision for robot policy pretraining. At its core, RynnLAM learns continuous, 3D-grounded latent actions from visual transitions without requiring native robot controls. By combining residual future-feature prediction, camera-compensated 3D-flow supervision, and camera-motion decoupling, RynnLAM encourages representations that capture control-relevant motion rather than appearance changes alone. We apply RynnLAM to 30.1K hours of human, robot, and simulation videos, producing 745.52M latent-action descriptors. RynnVLA-Latent then learns to predict latent-action chunks from visual observations and language through flow matching, before adapting its pretrained backbone and action expert to embodiment-specific robot actions. The resulting 4B policy achieves 98.8% success on LIBERO, 84.7% on LIBERO-Plus without benchmark-specific adaptation, 51.9% average success across five VLABench tracks, and 88.6% average success on the RoboTwin 2.0 bimanual benchmark. It also achieves the highest observed success rates among the compared methods on six real-world manipulation tasks across dexterous-hand and mobile-gripper platforms. Together with representation ablations and data-scaling results, these findings demonstrate the potential of latent-action supervision for scaling robot policy learning beyond native action-labeled data.

items.title: Security, (B)Orders, Technopolitics
items.abstract: This chapter lays out the conceptual framework for analyzing the technopolitics of Research and Development (R&D). It starts by situating R&D within ideas of borders as instruments of bifurcation and filtering, but also sites of sovereignty and statehood. The chapter discusses ideas of ‘orders’ that shape the practicing of R&D and sets forth the conceptualization of borders as processual, infrastructural and spatial. It discusses the concept of ‘security’ as not fixed, but rather as materialization of power relations which define threats, risks and insecurities. Following wider debates about ‘ordering’, the chapter presents the concept of ‘borderwork’ as the main framework of analysis, situating R&D in the processual understanding of borders. This allows for an understanding of manifold practices of R&D as formative of borders and orders. To this end, the chapter discusses the relationship between borderwork and approaches to practices informed by International Political Sociology (IPS). To make sense of the visions and ideas that shape the borderwork of R&D, the chapter focuses on the concept of imaginaries. The more specific idea of ‘sociotechnical imaginaries’ serves as a departure point to more broadly conceive of visions as formative of politics. Through this, the chapter critically engages with problematic structures of border security shaping R&D.

items.title: Self-Evolution Reasoner: Continuous Optimization via Policy-Intrinsic Exploration and Exploitation
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) enables large language models (LLMs) to continuously self-improve their reasoning capabilities. Compared to RLVR's scalar rewards, recent self-supervised on-policy distillation methods leverage denser supervision signals. However, both paradigms suffer from exploration bottlenecks, struggling to escape local optima when the policy fails to sample valid solutions. Relying on external demonstrations can bypass this issue; however, the off-policy nature hinders genuine self-improvement and the mismatched-distribution reasoning can not be fully exploited. In this work, we propose Self-Evolution Policy Optimization (SEPO), a framework that drives continuous reasoning capability evolution via guided exploration and in-distribution exploitation. Specifically, SEPO utilizes labels to elicit correct reasoning from the policy, unlocking the exploration potential. By treating current policy conditioned on this in-distribution reasoning as a self-teacher, SEPO distills the newly discovered solution back into the policy. Through this iterative cycle of policy-intrinsic exploration and exploitation, SEPO achieves robust and continuous capability evolution. Across scientific, tool-use, and complex logical reasoning domains, SEPO consistently achieves the best performance under identical training time or steps, demonstrating superior efficiency and convergence ceilings. Notably, SEPO maintains stable improvements even in scenarios where baselines severely underperform or fail entirely, such as on complex tasks or with small-scale models. Our code is available at https://github.com/Eric8932/SEPO.

items.title: Self-Management in Preventing Quiet Quitting through Career Readiness among Generation Z University Students
items.abstract: Quiet quitting has increasingly been discussed as a form of psychological disengagement characterized by minimum effort and limited initiative, including among Generation Z preparing to enter the workforce. This study examines whether career readiness mediates the relationship between selfmanagement and quiet quitting among students of the Faculty ofIslamic Economics and Business, Universitas Islam Negeri Sumatera Utara. A quantitative explanatory-correlational design was applied to 91 active students of the 2022 cohort, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a fivepoint Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS. Self-management had a significant positive effect on career readiness and a significant negative effect on quiet quitting. Career readiness, however, had no significant direct effect on quiet quitting and did not mediate the relationship between selfmanagement and quiet quitting. These findings indicate that selfmanagement reduces quiet quitting mainly through a direct pathway. Theoretically, the study highlights the central role of internal self-regulation; practically, it suggests that universities should strengthen students’ self-management, time management, and intrinsic motivation to sustain engagement and career preparation.

items.title: SentryBench: A Cost-Sensitive Benchmark for Adversarial Robustness of Tool-Using LLM Agents in Public-Safety Deployments
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly wired to consequential tools that send public alerts, dispatch responders, and query citizen records, where one erroneous tool call carries real-world cost. Existing agent-safety benchmarks measure generic harm or prompt-injection success and implicitly treat refusing as the safe default. In public-safety deployments that assumption breaks: an agent too cautious to dispatch help fails as surely as one that triggers a false alert. We present SentryBench, which scores agents on a two-sided, cost-sensitive frontier jointly measuring attack success, over-refusal (missing a real emergency), and over-reaction (unwarranted action) under adversarial tool use, with scenarios grounded in real emergency-call transcripts, disaster messages, and real injection/jailbreak payloads. We formalize deployment harm as an asymmetric cost functional, prove naive caution is harm-dominated whenever it refuses more genuine emergencies than the attack harm it averts, and prove a targeted trust gate adds zero over-refusal on clean input. Across 840 scored episodes over three frontier models and three defenses, refuse-more caution drives over-refusal to 100 percent on two of three models for at most a 3.7-point change in attack success and yields the worst harm everywhere, whereas our trust-gating wrapper dominates the frontier (lowest harm on every model, over-refusal at or below baseline, higher containment). Provider content filters also silently perform part of the defending and must be reported separately.

items.title: Shaping Future Automated School Bus Systems: Multi-Stakeholder Insights Informing Human-in-the-Loop Design
items.abstract: Although automation has been widely studied in private vehicles and public transit, the design of automated school buses has received limited attention. Little is known about how to address the concerns of adolescents, parents, and school bus drivers or how to translate them into interaction design. To fill these gaps, we conducted interviews and co-design workshops with multi-stakeholders. Based on concerns about current school buses and acceptance of automation revealed in the interview, we co-designed human-in-the-loop systems reflecting the participants’ view that high automation is acceptable only under human supervision. We proposed age-appropriate interaction principles with minimized adult-delivered messages when necessary. We also designed guardian interfaces that adapt across routine and emergency scenarios, with onboard systems coordinating cross-device tasks and remote systems enabling direct control and assistance in collaboration with onboard guardians. These designs move beyond conventional paradigms by embedding scenario-adaptive, multi-role collaboration mechanisms tailored to school transportation.

items.title: Sparse Sum-of-Squares Layers for Certified Learning
items.abstract: A central limitation of modern machine learning systems is the lack of formal certificates guaranteeing their behavior beyond empirical, sample-based evaluation. Sum-of-squares (SOS) methods provide such guarantees by certifying polynomial inequalities over continuous domains via semidefinite programming (SDP). While prior work has introduced SDP layers as differentiable components in neural networks, repeated learning calls can lose the computational benefit of the forward program's sparse representation. We propose Sparse SOS Layers, differentiable value layers whose backward passes reuse the local coordinates of the forward solve. Under a fixed template and learned objective coefficients, each layer avoids building dense certificates and reuses its sparse structure across training steps. Compared with existing methods, our approach achieves up to 2.7 times speedup in total warm-call time, with nearly 100 times lower memory usage (1.7 vs. 160 GiB) for relatively large problem sizes for the tested dense parameterization. Experiments cover sparse polynomial certification, pendulum control, combinatorial relaxations, robotics projection, oscillator chains, and pose graph synchronization. A design study achieves zero certified violations across unseen problem instances and sizes, while requiring roughly 7 times fewer optimization solves than estimating gradients by perturbing the objective coefficients and re-solving the problem (finite differences). These results show that sparse certificate values can be effectively integrated into learning pipelines when the backward pass respects the verifier's structure.

items.title: SpeC2Rust: Specification-Driven Repository-Level C-to-Rust Translation
items.abstract: Legacy C codebases remain central to system software and performance-critical infrastructure, but their weak memory safety imposes security and maintenance risks. Recent C-to-Rust translation systems, including LLM-based translators, make automated migration increasingly feasible, yet they still struggle to recover repository-level intent, avoid raw pointers and unsafe constructs, maintain cross-file interfaces, and repair compilation and validation failures efficiently. We propose SpeC2Rust, a specification-driven pipeline for repository-level C-to-Rust translation. It has three stages: (1) Project-Intent Structuring, which decomposes a C repository into semantically coherent modules and generates persistent repository- and module-level specifications; (2) Spec-Guided Generation, which translates each Rust module against these specifications with a live symbol registry to preserve cross-file consistency; and (3) Layered-Feedback Repair, which batches repairs and injects only failure-relevant diagnostics, specification context, and source evidence for efficient compilation and test-driven correction. We evaluate SpeC2Rust on eight repository-level C projects. It generates Rust projects that compile and pass the original end-to-end tests, with no raw-pointer declarations, raw-pointer dereferences, or unsafe lines. On projects shared with an LLM-based baseline, SpeC2Rust reduces cost by 66.1% and input-token usage by 84.7%.

items.title: SRA: Selective Residual Adaptation for LLM Reasoning Enhancement
items.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers reasoning capabilities from large language models to lightweight students. However, distilled small models still struggle with multi-step reasoning. We observe that the distribution divergences between teacher and student models along reasoning paths are highly sparse, and target tokens almost always fall within the student top-$K$ candidate set. Based on this finding, unlike approaches updating student backbones or requiring runtime teacher computation, we propose Selective Residual Adaptation (SRA), a plug-and-play framework that internalizes localized corrections. Concretely, SRA employs a Discrepancy Gate to identify divergence positions alongside a Candidate Residual Adapter for top-$K$ logit calibration to correct the mismatch. Theoretically, we establish error bounds ensuring strict sequence level performance gains. Across mathematical benchmarks on Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 4B, SRA consistently enhances distilled student models, raising average Pass@16 by up to 4.37 percentage points while preserving general capabilities.

items.title: Stability of Tenure: Is Contractualization a Cure?
items.abstract: The library profession has evolved from being traditional bookkeepers to being modern end users of digital data and Artificial Intelligence (AI), over the years. But throughout development, libraries are facing a major crisis: a severe shortage of permanent staff. Administrative bodies are hiring outsourced and temporary staff for most of their work to maintain daily functions as much as possible. This paper critically evaluates the trend of contract hiring, under the title “Stability of Tenure: is contractualization a cure? “However, contract hiring may be a fast & temporary remedy to the problem of vacant positions, but it is disaster to the core essence of the library profession. The libraries need highly skilled, permanent experts to manage complex tasks, relying on temporary staff risks the dignity of profession and user trust. The paper concludes by urging policymakers to invest in stable, permanent jobs to protect the future of libraries.

items.title: StemGuard : An Expertise‐Reinforced and Voice‐Controlled Agent for Stem Cell Culture Surveillance
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Vitro stem cell culture is vital for developing antiaging and antiallergy drugs. Cell confluence acts as a core indicator of cell proliferation and culture status. However, confluence estimation mostly depends on manual labour, as there are few artificial‐intelligence (AI) models or professional software developed for the task. Although most existing AI works adopted cell segmentation networks for confluence estimation, their efficacy and efficiency need improving. Meanwhile, the growth status of the cells is daily monitored with their images captured and archived by technicians using microscopes. As a result, cell images are constantly generated, exhibiting large data variance and posing challenges to the estimation models. Therefore, we propose StemGuard, perhaps the novel whole‐process AI agent specified at cell confluence estimation. It completes the basic confluence estimation task by a novel backbone that leverages categorization and feature fusion. It features an expertise‐reinforced optimization mechanism, which enables adaptive learning on the dynamic data. It also includes a voice control module for better use experience in sterile laboratories. In addition, we define a novel index, Average Confusion Degree (ACD), to assess confluence estimation. It measures the confluence error range rather than the raw error, as the former is more meaningful than the latter to the technicians. Evaluated on real microscopic cell images provided by a drug company, StemGuard runs smoothly and delivers state‐of‐the‐art cell confluence estimation performance, achieving an ACD of 0.0421 and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0638.

items.title: Stress Less by Design: Evaluating Usability and Stress Relief in a Self-Care App
items.abstract: As mobile self-care applications become increasingly common, understanding how their usability shapes emotional outcomes is essential. Prior research shows that self-care apps can reduce stress, but their effectiveness often depends on user engagement and adherence, which are strongly influenced by usability. Although poor usability is a frequent reason for disengagement, little is known about how users’ perceptions of usability relate to stress-reduction efficacy. The present study examined whether perceived usability predicted post-task distress, worry, and task engagement during a self-care exercise. Participants completed pre- and post-task stress measures and rated the app’s usability. While stress and worry decreased overall, usability showed a more complex pattern that contradicted hypotheses: higher usability predicted greater post-task distress, and this effect strengthened among participants with higher pre-task engagement. These findings highlight that effective self-care app design requires not just high usability, but usability that adapts to users’ engagement levels to maximize real-world therapeutic impact.

items.title: Student Engagement and Trust Calibration With Generative AI in a 5S Safety Assessment
items.abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used in engineering and technology education, but its role in safety education remains underexplored. This study examined undergraduate students’ ( N = 14) human-AI interaction during a 5S workplace safety assessment in a Human Factors course. Using a mixed-methods design, we analyzed User Engagement Scale–Short Form (UES-SF) responses and qualitative reflections after students independently completed a hazard identification task and compared findings with a parallel AI-generated assessment (ChatGPT-4o). Results revealed high perceived reward and value, minimal usability barriers, and mixed focused attention, suggesting task engagement without deep immersion. Qualitatively, students described AI as expanding hazard awareness, improving analytical structure, and accelerating information retrieval, while consistently emphasizing the necessity of human oversight and cautioning against overreliance. Integrated findings position generative AI as a human-in-the-loop decision-support tool: effective for scaffolding systematic reasoning and broadening hazard recognition, but insufficient as a substitute for domain-informed judgment.

items.title: Student Learning and Creativity in the Pre-AI and AI-Assisted Era
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has entered classrooms faster than the evidence needed to judge its educational value. Most published work so far reports gains in task performance, speed, and perceived personalisation, while far less attention has been paid to what happens to the qualities that education exists to build: the ability to think without assistance, to produce original ideas, to solve unfamiliar problems, and to understand concepts deeply enough to transfer them. This paper develops the research foundation and the research contribution for a study that compares student learning and creativity in the pre-AI era and the AI-assisted era. Drawing on cognitive offloading theory, the desirable difficulties and productive failure literatures, sociocultural theories of scaffolding, selfdetermination theory, and the componential model of creativity, the paper argues that the educational effect of GenAI depends less on whether students use it than on the cognitive role it plays: a substitute that performs the thinking, or a scaffold that supports the student in performing it. The paper contributes (1) an integrative Cognitive Role of AI framework that links patterns of AI use to learning and creativity outcomes through four mechanisms, (2) a set of testable propositions about moderation by educational level, field of study, and frequency of use, (3) a convergent mixed-methods design that combines cohort comparison, a controlled experiment, and a paired studentteacher perception study, and (4) a practice-oriented model of responsible AI use for teachers and institutions. No empirical results are reported; the paper is a theory-building and protocol contribution intended to guide and justify the forthcoming data collection.

items.title: STUDENT LEARNING USING AI
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored as a way to make digital learning more responsive to students’ individualneeds. This paper proposes an AI-assisted student learning system that combines learner preferences, topic-level progress, practiceresponses, and teacher feedback to recommend suitable learning resources and next-step activities. The proposed framework includesa learner interface, a content repository, a recommendation and feedback engine, progress analytics, and teacher oversight. Ratherthan treating a single score as a complete picture of ability, the system uses repeated learning evidence to identify topics that mayneed revision and to suggest practice at an appropriate level. The design emphasizes explainable recommendations, privacy,accessibility, and human supervision. A prototype could be developed using a web interface, a structured content store, and rulebased or machine-learning components selected according to available data. Evaluation should measure recommendation relevance,consistency, usability, learner engagement, and learning outcomes through a controlled and ethically approved study. Noexperimental performance is claimed in this conceptual paper; the framework and evaluation plan are presented for futureimplementation.

items.title: StudyGenAI: A Comprehensive Review of Multimodal Generative AI and Spaced Repetition in Modern EdTech
items.abstract: Traditional education heavily relies on passive reading from static textbooks and unstructured handwritten notes, leading to inefficient study habits and poor long-term retention. This review explores the paradigm shift from standard Learning Management Systems (LMS) to AI-driven educational platforms. We review the integration of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Multimodal Optical Character Recognition (OCR), and the SuperMemo-2 (SM-2) spaced repetition algorithm to facilitate active recall. Finally, we propose the architecture for 'StudyGenAI,' a platform designed to automate student revision and weakness tracking.
